preconditions.description: Input n is an integer between 1 and 100000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(color) <= k for color in stdout.split()[1:])
postconditions.description: Each color in the output is an integer between 1 and k (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.split()) == 2 and stdout.split()[0].isdigit() and all(c.isdigit() for c in stdout.split()[1:])
postconditions.description: Output consists of exactly two lines: the first line is k (number of colors), and the second line contains n space-separated color integers.

postconditions.expression: k == min(k for k in range(1, n+2) if all((i+1 != j+1 or (not any((i+1) % (j+1) == 0 and (j+1) in primes and (i+1) // (j+1) == (i+1) // (j+1) for j in range(n) if (j+1) in primes)) or (j+1 != i+1 or (not any((j+1) % (i+1) == 0 and (i+1) in primes and (j+1) // (i+1) == (j+1) // (i+1) for i in range(n) if (i+1) in primes))) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if colors[i] == colors[j])))
postconditions.description: The output k is the minimum number of colors such that no two jewelry pieces with prices p and q (where p is a prime divisor of q or vice versa) share the same color. Here, colors is the list of color assignments for each jewelry piece.
The second line contains exactly n color integers, one for each jewelry piece.
